runner_dissent: Two-sided dissent, honest. CAUTION side (the stronger flag): there is a real case to WAIT ONE DAY rather than open a starter now. The Q4 FY26 print + 10-K -- the exact event that would close O2/O3/O4 -- lands 2026-07-29 after close, and FOMC/Warsh is the same day; buying blind into a double binary, in a fresh-semiconductor-crash / AI-capex-audit regime, when the base-case IRR (~9.1%) only modestly clears the 8% hurdle and MOS has thinned to ~10%, is arguably imprudent when 24h of patience resolves the core uncertainty. A defensible alternative verdict is WATCH-through-the-print. I did NOT take it because (a) the methodology explicitly rejects treating uncertainty as a veto -- a STARTER is precisely the small-sliver test for 'want in but uncertain', (b) the print could gap UP and remove the entry, so waiting has its own cost, and (c) MSFT remains the relative pick of the Mega7 (the only name with a positive MOS + net cash + one-share-one-vote). I resolve it by KEEPING STARTER for direction but trimming the initial to 3% (from 4% at 6/19) and explicitly recommending a staggered entry around the print. UPSIDE side: net cash, one-share-one-vote, dividend, RPO $627B (+99%), the OpenAI $250B Azure backstop, and cheaper-memory-as-cost-tailwind could justify holding the 4% initial -- but I stay at 3% because two genuine gaps (O2 capex split, O3 OpenAI margin/attribution) remain open and a binary is 24h out. The single biggest unverified dependency is still O2: the entire owner-earnings base ($112B) rests on a ~40%-of-capex-is-growth assumption, and the capex-audit regime raises the cost of being wrong on exactly that. Existing holders: downgraded ADD->HOLD purely because price rose +3.7% out of the back-up-the-truck zone and a binary is imminent -- no sell trigger fired.
